learning_outcomes.text: Teach the physical concepts of the mechanics of point particles, rigid bodies and fluids, with particular emphasis on biomedical applications and expertise in physical principles of biological phenomena.
Enable the student to solve problems of physics concerning the aforementioned topics.
Develop critical analysis skills using examples of problems.

syllabus_topics: Motion in two and three dimensions
Concept of work and work done by a force
Gravitational force and the work done by it
Newton's second law in angular form
Equilibrium conditions for a rigid body
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written part and an oral part. If the score obtained is less than 18/30, the exam is not passed and must be repeated in its entirety. If the written score is 18/30 or higher, it is supplemented by an oral examination. If after the oral examination the grade is lower than 18/30, the exam (including the written part) must be repeated in its entirety. To pass, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of all course topics, apply basic principles to concrete examples, and use appropriate technical language.
bibliography: D. Halliday, R. Resnick, J. Walker - Fondamenti di Fisica - Meccanica, Onde, Termodinamica, elettromagnetismo, Ottica -Settima Edizione- Casa Editrice Ambrosiana
